WorkspaceSources.title: Mapping of Workspace Data Sources
WorkspaceSources.description:
`[workspace.sources.<name>]` holds definitions that a member uses with
`[sources.<name>] workspace = true`. A definition cannot itself inherit.

respect-ignore-files.description:
Respect `.gitignore` / `.ignore` and hidden-file filters while
discovering this source's files.

Respect `.gitignore` / `.ignore` and hidden-file filters while
discovering this source's files.

allOf.description: With `lint = "off"` the source is neither linted nor type-checked, so an override's `lint` or `check` would have no effect: it is an error.
With `check = "off"` the source is not type-checked, so an override's `check` would have no effect: it is an error.

SourceConnection.title: Source Connection
SourceConnection.description:
Where unqualified object names of this source resolve. `schema` requires
`database`.

database.description: Default database name, or the environment variable that supplies it.

schema.description:
Default schema name, or the environment variable that supplies it.
Requires `database`.

role.description: Role the source's sessions connect as, or the environment variable that supplies it; it resolves "$user" in search_path. Omitted (or "$user") means unknown.

ConnectionValue.title: Connection Value
ConnectionValue.description:
A literal string, or `{ env, default }` read from the environment when the
source is analyzed. When `env` is unset and `default` is omitted, analysis
of the source is skipped with an error.

env.description: Name of the environment variable. Must not be empty.

default.description: Value used when the variable is not set. Must not be empty.

FormatConfig.description: A source's or override's `format`: `"off"`, or `{ rules = { ... } }`.

FormatOptionsTable.title: Formatter options
FormatOptionsTable.description: A source's `format` takes only `rules`; formatter settings live in `sources.<name>.format.rules`.

rules.title: Formatter rules
rules.description:
Formatter settings of a source over the defaults; an override
`format = { rules = { ... } }` overrides them key by key (`case` by category).

case.title: Case rules for SQL tokens and identifiers
case.description: Groups case policies for identifiers, keywords, data types, and function names.

indent-style.title: Indentation character style
indent-style.description:
- `space`: use spaces
- `tab`: use tabs

This affects indentation at clause boundaries and multiline lists.

```sql
SELECT
    id
FROM
    users;
-- ^ this indentation uses spaces or tabs
```

indent-width.title: Indentation width per nesting level
indent-width.description:
This option is applied when `indent-style = "space"`.

```sql
SELECT
    id
FROM
    users;
-- ^ width = 4 example
```

line-width.title: Maximum target line width
line-width.description:
Formatter tries to keep lines within this width by moving lists/clauses to multiline when needed. When omitted (null), the input's line breaks are kept: each production stays flat or broken as written. When a number is given, lines are folded to fit that width.

```sql
-- narrow line-width
SELECT
    id,
    name
FROM
    users;

-- wide line-width
SELECT id, name FROM users;
```

line-ending.title: Line ending style
line-ending.description:
- `auto`: use CRLF when the raw source contains CRLF; otherwise use LF
- `lf`: always use LF
- `crlf`: always use CRLF

Formatter-preserved token content, such as multiline string literals,
remains byte-exact. When an embedded formatter rewrites a token body,
this policy applies to the line breaks generated in that body.

statement-blank-lines.title: Blank lines between statements
statement-blank-lines.description:
Accepts an exact count, or a table with an inclusive `minimum` and/or
`maximum` bound.

comment-blank-lines.title: Blank lines around comments
comment-blank-lines.description:
An integer applies to both sides. A table can configure `before` and
`after` independently; each side accepts the same exact-count or
inclusive-limit form as `statement-blank-lines`.

trailing-comma.title: Trailing comma policy
trailing-comma.description:
One policy for every place the SQL dialect accepts a trailing comma.
A dialect with no such place (PostgreSQL) ignores it. Today the only
place is Snowflake's SELECT column list, which accepts
`SELECT a, b, FROM t`.

- `preserve`: keep the input as written.
- `remove`: always remove it.
- `multiline`: add it when the list is broken across lines, remove it
  when the list fits on one line.
- `magic`: an existing trailing comma keeps the list multiline and is
  kept; a list without one never gains one (default).

Independently of this setting, the formatter removes an extra trailing
comma from a list that does not accept one.

column-alignment.title: Align CREATE TABLE columns
column-alignment.description:
When a CREATE TABLE column list is written over several lines, start the
types at one column and the first constraints at another, each as far right
as the longest name and the longest type need. Only the starts of the
name, the type and the constraints line up: the text inside a constraint
follows with single spaces, and a constraint wrapped by `line-width`
continues at the constraint column. A list that fits on one line and the
table constraints are not aligned. With `indent-style = "tab"`, only the
indentation is tabs; the alignment is spaces. Hover and completion show
the column lists of the document the same way.

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id          UUID   NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  note        TEXT
);
```

identifiers.title: The case style for unquoted SQL identifiers
identifiers.description:
Controls general identifiers such as database, schema, table, column,
and alias names. Quoted identifiers preserve their source spelling.

```sql
-- lowercase
SELECT account_id FROM analytics.daily_accounts;

-- uppercase
SELECT ACCOUNT_ID FROM ANALYTICS.DAILY_ACCOUNTS;
```

keywords.title: The case style for SQL keywords
keywords.description:
Controls tokens like `SELECT`, `FROM`, `WHERE`, `INSERT`, `RETURNING`.

```sql
-- lowercase
select id from users;

-- uppercase
SELECT id FROM users;
```

datatypes.title: The case style for SQL data types
datatypes.description:
Controls tokens like `INT`, `VARCHAR`, `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`.

Accepts either a single case style applied to built-in data types, or
a table that splits the policy between built-in and user-defined types.

```sql
-- lowercase
SELECT now()::timestamp with time zone;

-- uppercase
SELECT now()::TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE;
```

functions.title: The case style for function names
functions.description:
Applies uniformly to every function name (built-in and user-defined
alike). Unlike `datatypes`, this does not split by built-in vs.
user-defined: distinguishing them requires a per-dialect catalog of
known built-in function names, which formatters working from a single
file without semantic resolution do not have.

LowerCaseStyle.description: Wrapper around `CaseStyle` for fields that default to lowercase.

UpperCaseStyle.description: Wrapper around `CaseStyle` for fields that default to uppercase.

CategoryCaseRule.description:
Case policy for data types.

Accepts either a single [`CaseStyle`] applied uniformly, or a table that
splits the policy between built-in and user-defined names.

```toml
# uniform: applies to every data type name
[format.case]
datatypes = "uppercase"

# split: built-in uppercase, user-defined lowercase
[format.case.datatypes]
built-in = "uppercase"
user-defined = "lowercase"
```

anyOf.description: A single case style applied to both built-in and user-defined names.
Separate case styles for built-in and user-defined names.

CategoryCaseSplit.title: Split case styles for built-in vs user-defined names

built-in.title: Case style for built-in (dialect-provided) names
built-in.description:
Applies to names provided by the SQL dialect, such as built-in
functions (`count`, `now`) or built-in data types (`int`, `text`).

user-defined.title: Case style for names not recognized as built-in
user-defined.description:
Applies to every name the formatter does not recognize as built-in.
Working from a single file without type resolution, the formatter
cannot tell a genuine user-defined function/type from an unknown
name, so both fall into this bucket.

IndentStyle.title: The style of indentation
IndentStyle.description:
Whether to use spaces or tabs for indentation.

- `space`: Use spaces for indentation.
- `tab`: Use tabs for indentation.

IndentWidth.title: The number of spaces per indentation level
IndentWidth.description:
⚠️ **WARNING** ⚠️\
This option is only used when the indentation style is `space`.

LineEnding.title: Line ending style
LineEnding.description:
Controls the newline sequence generated by the formatter. Formatter-preserved
token content remains byte-exact. When an embedded formatter rewrites a token
body, this policy applies to the line breaks generated in that body.

oneOf.description: Use CRLF when the raw source contains CRLF; otherwise use LF.

BlankLineLimit.description:
A blank-line count, or an inclusive minimum/maximum limit.

The table form must contain at least one bound. When both are present,
`minimum` must not exceed `maximum`.

CommentBlankLines.description:
Blank-line limits adjacent to comments.

A single integer applies on both sides. The table form can configure the
`before` and `after` sides independently, and must contain at least one.

oneOf.description: Add it when the list is multiline, remove it otherwise.
Keep an existing trailing comma, which also keeps the list multiline.

PostgresLintOptions.title: PostgreSQL source linter options
PostgresLintOptions.description: The table form of a PostgreSQL source's or override's `lint`; it takes only `rules`.

rules.title: Lint rules for this source
rules.description:
Lint rule severities of a source (or of an override, over the source) rule by rule,
and also takes `allowed-parameter-styles`.

PostgresLintRules.title: PostgreSQL source lint rules
PostgresLintRules.description:
`allowed-parameter-styles` and a severity (`error` / `warn` / `ignore`)
per built-in lint rule.

allowed-parameter-styles.title: Allowed bind-parameter styles
allowed-parameter-styles.description: The bind-parameter placeholders this source's SQL may use.

no-select-star.description: Report `SELECT *`; list columns explicitly. Default is ignore (off).

limit-requires-order-by.description: Report `LIMIT` without `ORDER BY`, which returns nondeterministic rows. Default is warn.

union-quantifier-explicit.description: Report `UNION` without `ALL` or `DISTINCT`. Default is ignore (off).

duplicate-option.description: Report an option written more than once in one list where it may appear at most once. Default is warn.

duplicate-list-element.description: Report a list element written more than once where it may appear at most once. Default is warn.

update-requires-where.description: Report `UPDATE` without `WHERE`, which may update every row. Default is warn.

delete-requires-where.description: Report `DELETE` without `WHERE`, which may delete every row. Default is warn.

json-parse-error.description: Report a `json` / `jsonb` string constant whose type the statement writes (`'…'::json`, `CAST('…' AS jsonb)`, `json '…'`) and that PostgreSQL 16's input function rejects. The same code from a catalog-typed constant (an `INSERT` / `UPDATE` value, a function argument) comes from check and takes this severity too. PostgreSQL only: a Snowflake source accepts the key and reports nothing. Default is error.

TypeCheckOptions.description: A source's or override's `check`: `"off"`, or `{ rules = { ... } }`.

TypeCheckOptionsTable.title: Type checker options
TypeCheckOptionsTable.description: A source's `check` takes only `rules`; check rule severities live in `sources.<name>.check.rules`.

rules.title: Check rule severities
rules.description:
Check rule severities of a source over the defaults; an override
`check = { rules = { ... } }` overrides them rule by rule.

aggregate-function-context-mismatch.description: Report aggregate-only functions used outside valid SQL contexts. Default is error.

alias-column-count-mismatch.description: Report a table alias column list longer than the relation's columns. Default is error.

ambiguous-column.description: Report ambiguous column references. Default is error.

array-literal-malformed.description: Report an array string constant that PostgreSQL 16's array input function rejects. Default is error.

case-when-condition-type-mismatch.description: Report a `CASE WHEN` condition that is not boolean. Default is error.

cast-unresolved.description: Report a cast between types that has no cast. Default is error.

check-constraint-type-mismatch.description: Report a `CHECK` constraint condition that is not boolean. Default is error.

collation-not-supported-by-type.description: Report `COLLATE` applied to a type that has no collation. Default is error.

column-default-type-mismatch.description: Report a column `DEFAULT` whose type cannot be assigned to the column. Default is error.

common-value-type-mismatch.description: Report values that must share one type (`CASE` branches, `COALESCE`, `VALUES` columns, array elements) but have none in common. Default is error.

comparison-type-mismatch.description: Report incompatible types used in scalar comparisons. Default is error.

default-not-allowed.description: Report `DEFAULT` where PostgreSQL does not accept it. Default is error.

dropped-table.description: Report a read of a table an earlier `DROP` ended. Default is error.

duplicate-alias.description: Report a table name or alias written more than once in one `FROM`. Default is error.

duplicate-column.description: Report a column named more than once in one statement, or added to a table that has it. Default is error.

duplicate-relation.description: Report a `CREATE` of a relation that already exists. Default is error.

function-argument-count-mismatch.description: Report function argument count mismatches. Default is error.

function-argument-type-mismatch.description: Report function argument type mismatches. Default is error.

function-argument-value-mismatch.description: Report a constant function argument the function rejects (such as a date/time part the input type does not have). Default is error.

function-call-ambiguous.description: Report function calls that are ambiguous across supported overloads. Default is error.

function-not-immutable-in-context.description: Report functions that must be IMMUTABLE in the current SQL context. Default is error.

generated-column-write.description: Report a write to a generated column. Default is error.

group-by-ordinal-refers-to-aggregate-or-.description: Report GROUP BY ordinals that resolve to aggregate or window expressions. Default is error.

group-by-select-expression-not-grouped.description: Report SELECT expressions that are neither grouped nor aggregated. Default is error.

identity-column-state.description: Report an identity action on a column that cannot take it. Default is error.

insert-assignment-type-mismatch.description: Report an `INSERT` value whose type cannot be assigned to its column. Default is error.

insert-values-count-mismatch.description: Report INSERT VALUES count mismatches. Default is error.

invalid-literal-value.description: Report a typed string constant that the type's input function rejects. Default is error.

invalid-relation-ddl.description: Report relation DDL PostgreSQL refuses (such as a temporary relation in a non-temporary schema). Default is error.

invalid-view-column-list.description: Report a view column list longer than the view's columns. Default is error.

invalid-view-column-rename.description: Report a `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` that renames or reorders existing columns. Default is error.

join-predicate-type-mismatch.description: Report incompatible types used in JOIN predicate comparisons. Default is error.

json-duplicate-key.description: Report a `json` / `jsonb` string constant that names one object key twice. PostgreSQL accepts it (`jsonb` keeps the last value). Default is warn.

jsonpath-syntax-error.description: Report a `jsonpath` string constant that PostgreSQL 16's input function rejects. Default is error.

locking-clause-not-allowed.description: Report a locking clause (`FOR UPDATE` and the like) where PostgreSQL does not accept it. Default is error.

operator-ambiguous.description: Report an operator that is ambiguous for its operand types. Default is error.

operator-argument-type-mismatch.description: Report an operator that does not accept its operand types. Default is error.

parameter-type-mismatch.description: Report a bind parameter used as two incompatible types. Default is error.

parameter-type-undetermined.description: Report a bind parameter whose type cannot be determined. Default is error.

prefer-timestamptz.description: Report `timestamp` (without time zone) written as a type and suggest `timestamptz`. PostgreSQL only. Default is warn.

recursive-query-type-mismatch.description: Report a recursive query whose recursive term's column types differ from the non-recursive term's. Default is error.

scalar-subquery-column-count-mismatch.description: Report a scalar subquery that returns other than one column. Default is error.

set-operation-column-count-mismatch.description: Report set operation column count mismatches. Default is error.

set-operation-order-by-expression.description: Report an `ORDER BY` of a set operation that is not a result column. Default is error.

set-operation-type-mismatch.description: Report set operation columns that cannot coerce both sides to a common type. Default is error.

undefined-relation.description: Report a `DROP` or `ALTER` of a relation that does not exist. Default is error.

unknown-column.description: Report unknown column references. Default is error.

unknown-function.description: Report unknown function references. Default is error.

unknown-table.description: Report references to tables that are not defined across loaded SQL files. Default is error.

unsupported-alter-action.description: Report an `ALTER` action that cannot be performed on an existing relation. Default is error.

update-assignment-type-mismatch.description: Report an `UPDATE` value whose type cannot be assigned to its column. Default is error.

update-set-column-count-mismatch.description: Report UPDATE SET column/value count mismatches. Default is error.

values-order-by-aggregate.description: Report an aggregate in the `ORDER BY` of a bare `VALUES`. Default is error.

values-row-length-mismatch.description: Report `VALUES` rows of different lengths. Default is error.

window-function-context-mismatch.description: Report window-only functions used without OVER (...). Default is error.

wrong-object-type.description: Report a statement that names the wrong kind of relation (such as `DROP VIEW` of a table). Default is error.

MigrationOptions.title: Migration Files Configuration
MigrationOptions.description:
Narrows the set of source files that contribute DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP
TABLE, CREATE VIEW, CREATE FUNCTION, CREATE TYPE, CREATE INDEX, COMMENT)
to the schema registry. Files that do not match `include`/`exclude` are
still parsed and type-checked as queries, but any DDL they contain is
ignored.

When `include` is empty, the migration filter is disabled and every file
matched by the surrounding `sources.*.include`/`sources.*.exclude`
becomes a DDL source, preserving the previous behavior.

include.title: A list of migration files to include for DDL collection.
include.description:
The files are matched using the glob pattern syntax, evaluated
relative to the source root.

exclude.title: A list of migration files to exclude from DDL collection.
exclude.description:
The files are matched using the glob pattern syntax, evaluated
relative to the source root.

DbtOptions.title: dbt Relation Catalog
DbtOptions.description:
Reads the relations of one dbt project contained by the source root
from the manifest dbt generates. Both paths are relative to the
surrounding source root and must stay inside it; profiles, credentials
and environment variables are not configuration inputs.

project-root.description: Path to the dbt project root, relative to the surrounding source root.

manifest.description:
Path to the dbt manifest, relative to the surrounding source root
(not empty). Defaults to `<project-root>/target/manifest.json`.

SourceLineageConfig.description: A source's `lineage`: `"off"`, or the table of its `nagi lineage` settings. Overrides have no `lineage`.

SourceLineageTable.title: Source Lineage
SourceLineageTable.description:
The `nagi lineage` settings of one source: where its output (databases
and named queries) is written for external client generators, and how
its SQL files name queries.

output-files.description:
The `.json` files that `nagi lineage` writes this source's document to,
each relative to the `nagi.toml` that declares it. Every file gets the
same content, so clients in several languages can read one source's
lineage. Each file at most once; empty (the default) writes no file.

query-annotations.description:
The query annotation styles the source's SQL files may use to name a
query: `"nagi"` (`-- nagi: query getUser`, always on, so it must be
listed) and `"sqlc"` (`-- name: getUser :one`). Each style at most once.

QueryAnnotation.title: Query Annotation Style
QueryAnnotation.description:
A way to name a query in a SQL file: `"nagi"` is `-- nagi: query getUser`,
`"sqlc"` is sqlc's `-- name: getUser :one`.

PostgresSourceOverride.title: PostgreSQL Source File Override
PostgresSourceOverride.description:
Overrides the PostgreSQL source's `format`, `lint`, and `check` for files
matched by `include` and not matched by `exclude`. Each key is `"off"`
or the same table the source accepts; omitted keys fall back to the
source.

include.description: Glob patterns matched relative to the source root.

exclude.description: Glob patterns excluded relative to the source root.

SnowflakeLintOptions.title: Snowflake source linter options
SnowflakeLintOptions.description: The table form of a Snowflake source's or override's `lint`; it takes only `rules`.

rules.title: Lint rules for this source
rules.description:
Lint rule severities of a source (or of an override, over the source) rule by rule,
and also takes `allowed-parameter-styles`.

SnowflakeLintRules.title: Snowflake source lint rules
SnowflakeLintRules.description:
`allowed-parameter-styles` and a severity (`error` / `warn` / `ignore`)
per built-in lint rule.

allowed-parameter-styles.title: Allowed bind-parameter styles
allowed-parameter-styles.description: The bind-parameter placeholders this source's SQL may use.

no-select-star.description: Report `SELECT *`; list columns explicitly. Default is ignore (off).

limit-requires-order-by.description: Report `LIMIT` without `ORDER BY`, which returns nondeterministic rows. Default is warn.

union-quantifier-explicit.description: Report `UNION` without `ALL` or `DISTINCT`. Default is ignore (off).

duplicate-option.description: Report an option written more than once in one list where it may appear at most once. Default is warn.

duplicate-list-element.description: Report a list element written more than once where it may appear at most once. Default is warn.

update-requires-where.description: Report `UPDATE` without `WHERE`, which may update every row. Default is warn.

delete-requires-where.description: Report `DELETE` without `WHERE`, which may delete every row. Default is warn.

json-parse-error.description: Report a `json` / `jsonb` string constant whose type the statement writes (`'…'::json`, `CAST('…' AS jsonb)`, `json '…'`) and that PostgreSQL 16's input function rejects. The same code from a catalog-typed constant (an `INSERT` / `UPDATE` value, a function argument) comes from check and takes this severity too. PostgreSQL only: a Snowflake source accepts the key and reports nothing. Default is error.

SnowflakeSourceOverride.title: Snowflake Source File Override
SnowflakeSourceOverride.description:
Overrides the Snowflake source's `format`, `lint`, and `check` for files
matched by `include` and not matched by `exclude`. Each key is `"off"`
or the same table the source accepts; omitted keys fall back to the
source.

include.description: Glob patterns matched relative to the source root.

exclude.description: Glob patterns excluded relative to the source root.

anyOf.description: Inherit source settings from workspace-level configuration.

InheritWorkspaceSource.title: Inherit Workspace Data Source
InheritWorkspaceSource.description:
Uses `[workspace.sources.<name>]` as is. No other key is allowed; write
`lineage` and the other settings in the workspace definition.
